titulo: Future Forms: will / going to / present continuous
descripcion: At A2 you use going to for plans and will for quick decisions and predictions. The present continuous for fixed arrangements comes more fully at B1. This is the first step towards more precise time reference at higher levels.

filas: I'll help you. / It will rain.

ejemplos.texto: I'm going to study tonight after dinner.
I'm meeting her at six tomorrow.

notas: Going to is for something already decided or planned.
Will is for a decision made at the moment of speaking.
The present continuous can express the future with a time word, for arrangements.

contraste.es: El español usa voy a de forma muy parecida a going to, así que la estructura se transfiere directamente.

errores: Using will for something already planned.
Using going to for a spontaneous decision.

traducciones.de: Ich werde… / Ich habe vor, … zu…

redemittel.expresion: What are you going to do?

autochequeo: Is going to used for a plan?
Is will used for a spontaneous decision?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on going to versus will. Check whether each matches how planned the event is. Do not rewrite the text. Flag any confusion between the two. Flag anything unclear.
